mlvtoolbox

Documentation and articles: https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/

mlvtoolbox is an R package for measuring contour geometry and constructing reproducible visual stimuli from line drawings. It is an independently maintained R port and extension of the Bernhardt-Walther Lab’s Mid-Level Vision Toolbox, with pyMLV as an additional reference.

The aim is to make the original MLV methods available in R with explicit measurement choices, tested native performance improvements, and tools for matching stimulus sets. Where this package defines a measure differently from the original toolbox, for example so that junctions and branch scores do not depend on contour direction or on the start vertex of a closed contour, or so that each curvature turn is counted once, the package definition is the default and the published behaviour remains available through explicit mlv2023 options. Each difference is recorded, with a reproducer, in the differences register. Graph/design workflows are named extensions. Numerical equivalence is qualified against specific fixtures, not promised for every upstream output.

Purpose and differences · Credits and license audit · Measurement contract

Install locally

A C++17 compiler and Rcpp are required. From this repository:

install.packages("Rcpp")
install.packages(".", repos = NULL, type = "source")

Optional packages: xml2 for SVG, R.matlab for v5 MAT files, and png/jpeg for images. Python, Octave and model weights are not runtime dependencies.

Drawing to features

Contours are ordered matrices with columns x1, y1, x2, y2. Image coordinates increase rightward/downward; integer raster pixel centers start at (1,1). Subpixel coordinates are retained. Zero-length segments require explicit cleaning with zero_length=“drop”.

library(mlvtoolbox)
drawing <- mlv_drawing(
  list(rbind(c(5, 5, 35, 5), c(35, 5, 35, 25)),
       matrix(c(20, 1, 20, 30), nrow = 1)),
  width = 40, height = 35
)
drawing <- compute_contour_properties(drawing)
as.data.frame(drawing)             # segment measurements
drawing$junctions                  # positions, types, arms and angles
contour_statistics(drawing)        # long image-level histograms
feature_table(drawing)             # normalized contour-level predictors
plot_properties(drawing)

Histogram weighting and normalization are explicit: orientation/curvature collect segment length; length collects whole-contour length; junctions count events. A value within 1e-9 × max(1, |edge|) of a bin edge is binned as if on the edge, so mathematically equal angles share a bin on every platform. Normalized values are per 10,000 contour pixels. Valid zero scores remain distinct from missing scores.

How this port differs

  • An R workflow: drawing objects, feature tables and model compatibility metadata; Python and MATLAB serve as references.
  • Explicit method definitions: subpixel geometry, validated degeneracies and missingness, vertex-turning curvature by default (each turn counted once), an arc-length estimator at a stated scale, and physical calibration. estimator = "mlv2023" retains the published curvature.
  • Additional stimulus tools: constrained subset design and contour graph descriptors for closure, continuation and enclosure.
  • Measured implementation changes: compiled geometry and fused histograms, with performance and equality evidence.
  • Two modes for curvature, junctions and the medial axis: the package defaults, and explicit mlv2023 options that reproduce outputs the original lab computed in MATLAB (see parity evidence). No bundled SAM weights or MATLAB serialized models.

See the comparison with the originals for scope, source lineage and qualification boundaries.

Medial-axis analysis 

mask <- rasterize(drawing)
result <- analyse_mat(drawing, min_branch_points = 2)
plot(result$drawing, property = "parallelism")
scores <- contour_statistics(result$drawing, properties = "parallelism")
rgb <- render_drawing(result$drawing, property = "parallelism")

compute_mat() returns distances, nearest-boundary indices, AOF, skeleton, ordered branches, and method parameters. compute_mat_properties() adds parallelism, separation, mirror and optional taper ratings. map_mat_properties() transfers them back to contours.

By default the flux is pixel-centred and independent of how equidistant boundary pixels are labelled, the skeleton keeps no removable pixel, and branch scores do not depend on branch direction or numbering. The published-compatible recipe reproduces the lab’s stored MATLAB results: on 2,757 drawings, 99.1–99.4% of per-pixel scores agree within 1e-4 (residual: MATLAB’s single precision).

compat <- compute_mat(drawing, aof = "mlv2023", morphology = "hmt8",
                      branch_rule = "mlv2023",
                      threshold_angle = asin(0.3 * pi / 2) * 180 / pi)

These comparisons qualify computation against stored outputs, not the perceptual validity of the measures. See parity evidence and implementation status.

Manipulate and import 

parts <- split_contours(drawing, property = "curvature", fraction = 0.5)
rotated <- rotate_drawing(drawing, 30)
clipped <- clip_circle(rotated, radius = 15)
segmented <- segment_at_junctions(drawing)
regions <- split_junction_regions(drawing)

# Optional file adapters:
# drawing <- read_mlv_svg("drawing.svg")
# drawings <- read_mlv_mat("drawings.mat")
# traced <- trace_contours("black_lines_on_white.png")
# write_mlv_png(drawing, "drawing.png")

Both ranked groups obey their requested whole-contour length budgets; a middle contour can remain unassigned. Curvature means and integrated curvature have separate names. Geometry-changing operations invalidate derived results.

Model scoring accepts an R model/predict method or a function of a feature table. Bind the exact training table’s measurement schema before prediction:

features <- feature_table(drawing)
model <- bind_feature_model(function(z) z$length_1, features)
scores <- predict_contours(drawing, model)

The schema records predictor order, bin edges, weights, units and normalization. Prediction rejects missing or incompatible training metadata before calling the model. Use fixed length_range and curvature_range values when comparing drawings with different canvas sizes. A model can instead receive its training schema via expected_spec = feature_schema(features). The explicit legacy option check_spec = FALSE warns that compatibility was not checked.

trace_rgb() requires an explicitly supplied provider returning an ink mask. No SAM model/backend is bundled; arbitrary edge detectors are not silently substituted for SAM. MATLAB serialized regression models, general SVG paint effects and MAT v7.3/HDF5 import are outside the current adapters.

For reproducible measurements, use a fixed specification:

spec <- feature_spec(c("length", "curvature", "orientation"),
                     estimator = "arclength", curvature_scale = 2)
measured <- compute_contour_properties(drawing, spec = spec)
features <- feature_table(measured)

The default curvature estimator, turning, spreads each vertex turn over the half-segments on either side of it, so every turn is counted once; arclength smooths the turns at a stated scale. Both wrap closed contours. The published estimator, estimator = "mlv2023", counts the last vertex of every contour twice and depends on how a curve is sampled; use it to reproduce published values. Physical measurement uses units = "visual_degrees" with an explicit pixels_per_degree. New branch scores use branch_estimator = "arclength". See the measurement contract for definitions, migration, metadata, and the limits of raster resolution invariance.

Differences, provenance and storage

  • Differences from the reference implementations: stable IDs, executed reproducers, source findings and R regressions. No upstream reports have been submitted.
  • Source provenance: pinned source-only snapshots, retained-file checksums and reference-data custody.
  • Cleanup receipt: one verified shared collection at reference-data/mlv; about 2.63 GiB of logical duplicate/history storage removed.
  • tools/restore_upstream.py restores full original checkouts to an explicit new destination. Large reference data and vendor snapshots are excluded from the R package tarball.

Credits, citation and licenses

The original toolbox and methods are by Dirk Bernhardt-Walther, Delaram Farzanfar, Seohee Han, Morteza Rezanejad and the Bernhardt-Walther Lab. The R implementation and extensions are by Bradley Buchsbaum. We also credit Aravind Narayanan for the Python AOF reference, Josep Mones i Teixidor and Carnë Draug for the Octave morphology tables, and Peter Kovesi for retained edge-linking reference helpers. Full source and contribution details distinguish these roles.

Run citation("mlvtoolbox") to cite the R implementation and original methods. The R implementation is declared GPL-3.0-or-later; see COPYING. Upstream notices and credits are also included in the installed package.

Vendored sources retain their own terms: Python has an MIT root license with GPL notices in three files, while many MATLAB files have no explicit license grant. The audit records this unresolved permission issue; our GPL declaration does not relicense those files. Dataset and model redistribution rights are separate, and neither is asserted here.

Development

Run testthat::test_local() for behavior/numerical checks. The reference generation and upstream reproducer scripts are in tools/reference and tools/upstream. Local check results, benchmarks and cross-platform status are recorded separately.

For a bounded source build/check, use python3 tools/bounded_check.py. It stages only package files before invoking R, so retained reference data are not copied into the build workspace.
